function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of the most common ways you can get a cake delivered—whether you’re looking for something ready‑made, a custom creation, or just a convenient pick‑up option.

| Option | What it offers | How to use it | Tips |
|--------|----------------|---------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Freshly baked cakes, often customizable | Search “cake shop near me” or check Google Maps / Yelp listings. Call or visit their website to place an order. | Ask about flavor, size, and delivery window. Many small shops love to accommodate special requests. |
| **National chain bakeries** | Consistent quality, nationwide delivery | Examples: **Panera Bread**, **Cinnabon**, **Baker & Spice**. Order via their app or website. | Great for standard sizes; check if they offer same‑day delivery in your area. |
| **Online food‑delivery platforms** | Wide selection from many restaurants & bakeries | Apps: **Uber Eats**, **DoorDash**, **Grubhub**, **Postmates**. Search “cakes” or “desserts.” | Delivery fees vary; look for promotions or free delivery thresholds. |
| **Specialty dessert sites** | Gourmet or niche flavors (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free) | Sites: **Goldbelly**, **Etsy** (hand‑crafted cakes), **CakeBoss**. | Shipping may take a day or two; confirm shipping dates for events. |
| **Grocery delivery services** | Ready‑made cakes from supermarkets | Apps: **Instacart**, **Amazon Fresh**, **Shipt**. Search “birthday cake” or “cupcakes.” | Check if the store has a cake aisle; some deliver pre‑packaged cakes. |
| **Custom cake designers** | Fully personalized designs | Websites: **Bakeology**, **The Cake Shop**, or local Instagram accounts. | Provide design details early; expect higher prices for intricate decorations. |
| **Subscription boxes** | Monthly cake deliveries | Services: **Dessert Club**, **Cratejoy** (various cake boxes). | Good for regular treats; usually not event‑specific. |

### Quick steps to order:

1. **Decide on the type of cake** – ready‑made vs. custom, dietary restrictions, size, occasion.
2. **Choose a platform** – local bakery for freshness, delivery service for convenience, or specialty site for unique flavors.
3. **Place the order** – either through the bakery’s own website/app or via a third‑party delivery app. Make sure to specify pickup/delivery time, address, and any special instructions.
4. **Confirm payment & delivery** – most platforms accept credit cards, PayPal, or Apple Pay. Verify the estimated arrival time.
5. **Track the order** – many apps let you see real‑time updates. If you’re ordering a custom cake, keep in touch with the baker for any last‑minute changes.

---

#### Need help finding a specific bakery?

If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated local bakeries and their contact info. Or, if you’re looking for a particular style (vegan, gluten‑free, artisanal), let me know and I’ll narrow down the best options for you!
